content.title: Identifying Data Trends: Increases, Decreases, Peaks, and Plateaus
content.overview: This lesson focuses on analyzing how a dependent variable changes in relation to an independent variable. You will learn to identify specific patterns—rising, falling, peaking, or staying flat—across a sequence of data points to accurately describe overall trends.
learning_objectives: Identify increasing and decreasing segments in a dataset.
Recognize plateaus where values remain constant or nearly unchanged.
Locate peaks representing local maximum values.
Describe complex trends by sequencing contiguous segments in order.

sections.title: The Trend Cardinal Scan
sections.content:
To accurately identify a trend, use the Trend Cardinal Scan strategy. First, establish the order of the independent variable (usually on the x-axis or the first column of a table). Scan the values from left to right or earliest to latest. As you scan, look for contiguous segments where the values consistently move in one direction or stay the same. A 'rising' segment shows increasing values, a 'falling' segment shows decreasing values, and a 'plateau' occurs when values remain nearly equal over a range. A 'peak' is a specific point or short plateau that represents the highest value in a sequence, surrounded by lower values.

![A flowchart showing the steps to identify data trends: Mark Axis Range, Identify Segments, Label Longest Segment, and Final Sequence Check.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/9ab17ac4-c5fd-4fd7-8d2d-46d9e95cddb2-1786506546675-914.webp)

sections.title: Categorizing Data Segments
sections.content: Data rarely moves in a single straight line. Most ACT Science passages involve multi-part trends. An 'increasing' trend means the y-values are getting larger as x-values increase. A 'decreasing' trend means y-values are getting smaller. A 'plateau' is a flat region where the rate of change is zero or near-zero. When a trend changes direction from increasing to decreasing, the highest point reached is the 'peak'. When describing these, always prioritize the longest contiguous segment or the most pronounced change to ensure your description matches the overall pattern.

worked_examples.question: A scientist measures the temperature of a solution every 10 minutes. The recorded temperatures (in Celsius) are: 20, 35, 50, 50, 50, 42, 30. Describe the trend from 0 to 60 minutes.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Mark the order of the independent variable (Time: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 mins). Step 2: Identify segments. From 0 to 20 mins, values rise (20 to 50). From 20 to 40 mins, values stay at 50 (plateau). From 40 to 60 mins, values fall (50 to 30). Step 3: Sequence the labels. The trend is an initial increase, followed by a plateau, and ending with a decrease.

common_mistakes: Confusing a plateau with a peak: A peak is a single high point or the very top of a curve, while a plateau must stay flat for at least two consecutive measurement points.
Ignoring the independent axis order: Always read trends in the direction of the independent variable (usually left-to-right), not based on the magnitude of the numbers alone.
Overlooking small fluctuations: Focus on the 'contiguous' or overall movement rather than minor noise unless the question asks for specific point-to-point changes.
exam_tips: Look for the 'turning points' where a graph changes from rising to falling; these are your peaks.
If a question asks for the 'overall trend,' look for the pattern that covers the largest portion of the x-axis.
Use the 'finger-trace' method: move your finger along the graph from left to right and whisper 'up,' 'down,' or 'flat' to identify segments quickly.
content.recap: Data trends are described by breaking a sequence into segments of increase, decrease, plateaus, and peaks. By scanning the independent variable in order and labeling the longest contiguous segments, you can accurately characterize complex data patterns.

knowledge_claims.content: An increasing trend is defined by dependent variable values that consistently get larger as the independent variable increases.
A decreasing trend is defined by dependent variable values that consistently get smaller as the independent variable increases.
A plateau is a segment of a data trend where the values remain constant or nearly unchanged over a range of the independent variable.
A peak is a local maximum value in a dataset that is preceded by an increase and followed by a decrease.
The first step in the Trend Cardinal Scan is to identify the order of the independent variable, typically reading from left to right on a graph or top to bottom in a table.
A plateau is recognized in a table when two or more consecutive measurements of the dependent variable are identical or very similar.
When describing a complex trend, the segments must be listed in the chronological order of the independent variable.
It is a mistake to label a single high point as a plateau; a plateau requires a flat duration across a range of the independent axis.
To verify a trend description, confirm that the verbal labels (rise, fall, plateau) match the actual sequence of values in the data source.
The 'dominant pattern' in a dataset is usually the longest contiguous segment of a specific trend type (e.g., a long increase followed by a short peak).
A peak differs from a plateau in that a peak represents a change in direction (increase to decrease), whereas a plateau represents a period of no change.
A 'sharp peak' is characterized by a rapid increase immediately followed by a rapid decrease, with little to no time spent at the maximum value.

items.stem:
SCIENCE PASSAGE 6: Origins of Bright Crater Rays
Three students discuss why some young impact craters have bright rays extending across the surface.

Student 1: The rays consist mainly of fresh material excavated from beneath a dark, weathered surface. With time, exposure to radiation and tiny impacts darkens the rays until they resemble the surrounding ground.

Student 2: The material is not intrinsically brighter. Impact fragments roughen the surface, and the rough texture reflects sunlight toward the observer at certain angles. As small grains settle, the directional reflection weakens.

Student 3: Both excavation and texture matter. Fresh subsurface material begins brighter than the surface, and rough fragment deposits enhance that contrast. Weathering and settling therefore work together to fade the rays.

Which choice best describes a central difference between Student 1 and Student 2?

options.F: Student 1 emphasizes material composition, whereas Student 2 emphasizes surface texture.
options.G: They use identical explanations and disagree only about vocabulary.
options.H: Student 1 discusses an unrelated biological process, while Student 2 refuses to offer a mechanism.
options.J: Student 2 accepts every claim made by Student 1 without qualification.

items.explanation: The choice accurately contrasts the mechanisms emphasized by the two viewpoints.

items.stem:
SCIENCE PASSAGE 1: Enzyme Activity Across pH
Researchers measured the activity of an enzyme from two microorganisms across four buffer pH values. Equal enzyme concentrations and substrate amounts were used. Activity is reported as micromoles of product formed per minute.

Which series had the greater value at 10?

options.J: The figure does not contain values for that condition.

items.explanation: Compare the two plotted values at the final x-position.
